definition: Artificial intelligence (AI) and its subfields have been used in applications throughout industry and academia.
details: Machine learning has been used for various scientific and commercial purposes, including language translation, image recognition, decision-making, credit scoring, and e-commerce. Since the 2020s, massive advancements have been made in the field of generative AI (GenAI) as a result of the 2017 inception of Transformer Model architecture. GenAI has the ability to create text, images, voice, music, videos, and other forms of data from chat-based prompting.

explainer.lead: Applications of artificial intelligence are the practical ways AI is put to work in fields such as farming, software development, education, energy, and customer service. They matter because their value depends not just on model capability, but on whether they improve a real task without introducing errors, bias, or extra work.

tiers.eli5: AI is like a helper that can notice patterns, make predictions, or create things such as text and pictures. Different jobs need different helpers: one might spot where crops need water, while another answers questions about an order. People still need to check its work because a confident answer can still be wrong or unfair.
tiers.practitioner: In practice, AI is embedded in a domain workflow: code assistants plug into editors and IDEs, hiring systems screen and rank candidates, and monitoring systems analyze satellite, acoustic, or remote-sensing data. Generative systems use Transformer-based models for prompted creation, while other applications use machine learning or expert systems. Review outputs for correctness, security, bias, and technical debt; faster generation can be offset by debugging, testing, poor workplace content, and weak revenue results.
tiers.paperLevel: An AI application couples a learned or rule-based mapping f: X -> Y with a domain process, where X may contain text, images, speech, sensor data, or code and Y may be a prediction, ranking, decision aid, or generated artifact. Generative AI advanced rapidly in the 2020s following the 2017 inception of the Transformer architecture. Known limits include incorrect or inefficient code, replication of poor security practices, demographic bias in hiring, and generated work that appears useful without advancing the task.

explainer.example: A farmer uses AI to identify parts of a field that need irrigation, fertilization, or pesticide treatment. Those areas can then receive targeted treatment instead of treating the whole field uniformly, with the aim of increasing yields and improving efficiency.

usedIn.name: Agriculture
usedIn.detail: Identifying areas needing irrigation, fertilization, or pesticide treatment, and detecting diseases and pests.

usedIn.name: Software development
usedIn.detail: Editor and IDE plugins provide code completion, chat, and automated test generation.

usedIn.name: Customer service
usedIn.detail: Chatbots check or cancel orders, offer refunds, and connect customers with human representatives.

usedIn.name: Environmental monitoring
usedIn.detail: Global Plastic Watch uses satellite monitoring to analyze and track plastic waste sites.

explainer.intuition: The same broad set of AI techniques becomes an application only when connected to a particular job, its data, and the people acting on the result. The useful unit is therefore the whole workflow, not the model alone.
howItWorks: Choose a concrete task, such as grading, chip placement, irrigation planning, or answering customer requests.
Supply relevant domain inputs, including text, images, speech, code, or environmental observations.
Apply an AI approach, such as machine learning, generative AI, or an expert system, to produce a prediction, ranking, recommendation, or artifact.
Integrate that output into the existing service or work process.
Check its effects on quality, productivity, safety, fairness, and costs rather than assuming automation brings improvement.
explainer.whyItMatters: AI applications can automate repetitive work, support decisions, and help monitor systems at large scales. Their benefits are uneven, so deployment must account for errors, bias, collaboration, security, and whether the work genuinely improves.
misconceptions: Using AI automatically raises productivity or revenue; surveyed results and studies of workplace content show that this is not guaranteed.
AI-generated code is ready to ship; it can be incorrect, inefficient, insecure, or costly to debug and test.
Applications of AI are all generative AI; they also include expert systems, prediction, ranking, monitoring, and design automation.
